subject: Post-call: streaming UX & model-fit next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@brightwave.health>, Devon Chen <devon.chen@brightwave.health>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: streaming UX & model-fit next steps

Hi Olivia / Devon —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet the BrightWave team. Quick recap + concrete next steps to keep momentum:

Summary from our side:
- Primary goal: embed a streaming assistant into your clinician-facing triage UI with sub-300ms token latency for first tokens and coherent mid-sentence streaming (avoid half-sentence stops).
- Current pain: observed partial outputs (mid-sentence truncation), stop-sequence not consistently applied to third-party content, and occasional 600–900ms latency spikes in production traces you shared.
- Key constraints: PHI handling requirements, SOC2 evidence requested, and a low tolerance for hallucinations on patient-sensitive prompts.

Immediate recommendations we discussed (we'll prep a short Eval run):
1) Model variants for evaluation: rw-low-latency-7b (fast streaming baseline) and rw-high-fidelity-14b (quality baseline).
2) Streaming config: enable streaming=true, chunk_size_tokens=128, and use prefix/KV caching for repeated context windows.
3) Stop sequences: explicitly pass stop=["

", "
User:"] and add an explicit end-token marker in your prompt templates to avoid mid-sentence drops.
4) Prompt sets: we'll share a 50-sample prompt set derived from your call transcript (attached) and a set of negative examples for hallucination checks.
5) SLOs & monitoring: suggest token-level tracing and 95/99p latency dashboards; we can provide our Redwood Console trial view for your team.

Attachments: redwood-eval-benchmarks.csv (initial perf profile), brightwave-stream-transcript.txt (sample prompts you shared).

Next steps / owners:
- Ben (me): provision a 48-hour eval with the two model variants, upload prompt sets, and share a dashboard link by Tue 5/5 EOD.
- Laura (SE): run a quick streaming check to reproduce the mid-sentence truncation and test stop sequence behavior; share config diff.
- Olivia / Devon: confirm a sample 50-item prompt set and whether PHI will be redacted prior to upload.
- Rafael: will pick up procurement/contract Qs if we need a burst dedicated pool for strict SLAs.

Proposed follow-up: 30-min on Wed 5/6 10:00–10:30 PT to review results. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to the eval results.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@brightwave.health>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Chen <devon.chen@brightwave.health>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: streaming UX & model-fit next steps

Thanks Ben — quick responses inline.

Appreciate the summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- The partial output issue: the assistant often emits a newline and stops mid-clause (example lines attached). We suspect the client-side render treats a chunk boundary as completion.
- Stop sequence: we've been sending stop=["
"], which isn't robust for our templates; we can try the suggestions you listed.
- Latency spikes: we see spikes mostly between 2–4pm PT during clinical shift change; could be correlated with burst traffic hitting our VPC egress.

Security / compliance: we need a copy of SOC2 evidence and a short doc on how Redwood isolates KV cache and logs for private deployments. We attached a redacted transcript and a short list of our PHI handling rules.

We approve the 50-sample prompt set approach — I attached brightwave-stream-transcript.txt (redacted). Please go ahead with the eval.

Olivia
Olivia Park
Sr. Director, Clinical AI — BrightWave Health
olivia.park@brightwave.health | (617) 555-3344

Attachment: brightwave-stream-transcript.txt

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia.park@brightwave.health>, Devon Chen <devon.chen@brightwave.health>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 07:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: streaming UX & model-fit next steps — internal triage

Internal — please triage the streaming issues and prep the eval. Olivia approved the prompt set and attached transcript. Key asks below (short-term triage + eval plan):

What I want from the SE/infra side in the next 48 hours:
- Reproduce partial-output: run a streaming session against the transcript, capture token boundary logs, and confirm whether the client or runtime is producing premature end events. Include a minimal repro script.
- Stop-sequence test matrix: test stop variants ["

"], ["
User:"], ["<END>"] with both model variants. Note any differences in final_token detection across rw-low-latency-7b and rw-high-fidelity-14b.
- Latency profiling: pull 95/99p per-token latency from the last 7 days for the BrightWave VPC region; check for correlation with traffic windows.

Suggested configuration for the eval run (start asap):
- Models: rw-low-latency-7b (streaming baseline) + rw-high-fidelity-14b (quality baseline)
- Runtime flags: streaming=true, chunk_size_tokens=128, kv_cache=true, response_chunk_timeout_ms=80
- Prompt template: add explicit end marker "<END>" and set stop=["<END>", "

"]
- Metrics to capture: first_token_latency, per_token_p95/p99, streaming_coherence_score (we'll use our 0–100 rubric), hallucination_hits (binary).

Attachments to include for Olivia: redwood-eval-benchmarks.csv (initial perf profile) and a short SOC2 snippet: brightwave-soc2-qa.pdf (we'll attach sanitized SOC2 evidence relevant to isolation and logs).

Laura / Tessa — can you own the repro + run? Rafael — ping me if we need to fast-track a Dedicated pool for a multi-hour stress run.

Ben

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia.park@brightwave.health>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: streaming UX & model-fit-streaming-ux-action-items — SE plan + invite

Got it — taking lead on repro and stop-sequence matrix. Plan + ETA:
- Today (Mon 5/4): reproduce the truncation with a minimal Node repro against rw-low-latency-7b; capture token logs and client events. Deliverable: repro gist + logs by 5pm PT.
- Tue 5/5 morning: run the two-model eval against the 50-sample prompt set, collect metrics and populate the shared Drive doc.
- Wed 5/6 10:00 PT: join the customer review (Ben, Olivia, Devon). I created a tentative invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=brightwave-review-20260506

Quick note on stop sequences: in our experience, adding an explicit unique marker (e.g., <END>) in the prompt and sending it as a stop token is the most robust client/runtime-safe approach. If BrightWave cannot add markers, we'll instrument a client-side guard that waits for a trailing punctuation token before rendering 'final' state.

I’ll post results to: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/drive/brightwave-evals-2026 and link the HubSpot deal after the run.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
